bib.title: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Social Biases in Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021

read.skipped: References (chars ~44660-61441) and the Table 13/14 token lists only skimmed

question: How can sources of representational social bias in text generation be defined and measured, and can a pretrained LM be debiased post hoc without retraining while keeping context associations?
hypothesis: Dynamically finding bias-sensitive tokens and applying autoregressive nullspace projection mitigates local and global bias while retaining contextual information, improving the performance-fairness Pareto frontier.
contributions: Disentangle fine-grained local bias from high-level global bias in text generation, with metrics that separate bias association from context association
New benchmark of diverse real-world contexts (16,338 contexts from 5 corpora)
A-INLP: post-hoc debiasing of pretrained LMs using automatically found bias-sensitive tokens and autoregressive iterative nullspace projection

method.summary: Bias subspace from definitional word pairs (GloVe, PCA) yields bias-sensitive tokens; a linear SVM bias classifier on GPT-2 context embeddings is iterated to obtain a nullspace projection P; at each decoding step the output distribution mixes the projected and original distributions with weight alpha (tuned or learned per step). Applied to pretrained GPT-2 small with no retraining of the LM.
method.task: post-hoc social-bias mitigation in autoregressive text generation (gender, religion)

datasets.name: Diverse contexts (WikiText-2 first 10%, SST, Reddit, MELD, POM)
datasets.split: Bias classifier data: 6,000 contexts -> 2,940 train / 1,260 val / 1,800 test. LM performance: 50 random contexts per bias class; bias: 100 sampled contexts per class with swapped pairs
datasets.source: Public corpora plus Reddit forums on politics, electronics, relationships
datasets.preprocessing: Sentences with sensitive tokens from multiple classes removed; sentences under 5 tokens removed; random subsequence taken as context

datasets.name: Simple contexts (Sheng et al., 2019 templates)
datasets.preprocessing: XYZ placeholder replaced with definitional tokens

models.name: A-INLP (tune alpha / learn alpha) and A-SUBSPACE
models.architecture: post-hoc projection on GPT-2 context embedding

training.objective: Linear SVM (l2 penalty, squared hinge loss) classifying the protected attribute from context embeddings; iterated nullspace projection. GPT-2 itself is not trained.
training.epochs: Table 6: P trained for 30 and 15 epochs (two sets of rows)
training.dropout: swept 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 (selected value is in bold in the PDF, not recoverable from text)
training.hardware: Tesla P40 Ti GPU with 22 GB memory

other.nullspace_iterations: 80 classifiers for gender, 50 for religion; swept 40-90
other.hyperparameter_search: grid ranges in Tables 10 and 11; chosen values shown in bold in the PDF but lost in text extraction
other.SVM_sweep: C 0.1-10; penalty l1/l2; loss hinge/squared hinge; iterations 500-5000

inference.decoding: Sampling from the mixed distribution; top-k used to build V' for alpha_t (k not stated)
inference.max_tokens: maximum length swept 20-40; average generated sentence length 25
inference.prompting: Context prefixes (templates or corpus subsequences) with gender/religion terms swapped

parameters.alpha: swept 0.1-0.9 for A-INLP Tune alpha; alpha=1 recovers INLP; alpha=0 recovers GPT-2; alpha_t learned per step as p*-weighted mean of bias-subspace projection q(w) over top-k tokens intersected with S
parameters.embedding_for_subspace: GloVe (more accurate than GPT-2 embeddings, especially for religion)

other.inference_cost: 1.21 s and 1231 MiB per 25-token sentence vs 1.12 s and 1181 MiB for GPT-2; 102 s to load model and tokenizer

metrics.name: Local bias
metrics.definition: KL divergence or Hellinger distance between next-token distributions under counterfactual (gender/religion swapped) contexts

metrics.name: Global bias
metrics.definition: Absolute difference |g(s1)-g(s2)| of regard/sentiment classifier scores of sentences generated from swapped contexts

metrics.name: Context association / LM performance
metrics.definition: p(w*|c) for ground-truth word, plus KL/Hellinger to original GPT-2 distribution

metrics.name: StereoSet LM, SS, ICAT
metrics.definition: Language modeling score, stereotype score, idealized CAT score

metrics.name: Human evaluation
metrics.definition: Clarity, content, fairness rated 1-5 by 5 annotators

eval.protocol: Performance-fairness trade-off plots (Fig 3); StereoSet; 5 human annotators chosen for diversity of age, gender, race and religion. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests stated.

evidence.quote: SVM model has 2307 parameters (768 ∗3 + 3) and small GPT-2 has 124 million parameters.

results.note: Appendix D.5 says religion ICAT improves by 7% and gender by 3%, apparently describing the other A-INLP row; Table 6/16 values 74.27 -> 88.51 give about 19%

results.table: Table 6, row A-INLP (second set), column SS

results.claim: Diverse-context dataset size: 16,338 contexts (15,162 gender, 1,176 religion) from 948,573 sentences
results.quote: we collect a large set of 16,338 diverse contexts from 5 real-world text corpora

results.claim: Fixing the first sensitive token largely removes bias in the remaining text
Directly applying INLP (alpha=1) gets best fairness but hurts LM performance; GPT-2 is best on performance and least fair

limits: Authors: strong performance-fairness trade-offs; not a guarantee of real-world safety
Depends on one perception of bias (definitional pairs, subspace, classifier); may not generalise across cultures or time
Only binary-gender pairs for gender and three religions (Judaism, Christianity, Islam) were tested; only GPT-2 small
Hard to detect and mitigate bias in diverse real-world contexts; classifier data imperfect and nullspace removes context information
GPT-2 embedding subspace inaccurate; GloVe lacks many subword tokens
Human fairness gain is tiny in absolute terms (3.93 to 4.00); no seeds or significance tests reported; chosen hyperparameters not recoverable from text
Global-bias plots are not smooth, attributed to sampling stochasticity
Dated: GPT-2 small only; tokenwise linear projection evaluated before instruction-tuned LLMs

terms.definition: predictions generated at a particular time step that reflect undesirable associations with the context
representational differences across entire generated sentences spanning multiple phrases
Autoregressive iterative nullspace projection applied to the context embedding at each decoding step, mixed with the original distribution by alpha
